title: ORBIT: Offset-based Activation Steering for Cross-lingual Multimodal Fact Verification
abstract: arXiv:2611.27421v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multimodal fact verification faces a fundamental accessibility bottleneck: while large proprietary models exhibit cross-lingual robustness, small vision-language models suffer a severe, disproportionate accuracy collapse on low-resource languages. Closing this gap traditionally requires prohibitive scale or extensive language-specific fine-tuning. In this work, we propose Offset Recovery via Bilingual Inference-time Technique (ORBIT), an algorithmic intervention that mitigates this collapse at inference time. ORBIT estimates span-specific offset vectors from parallel claim-evidence instances and applies them to claim and evidence representations, targeting the cross-lingual degradation induced by low-resource evidence. translated_title: ORBIT：面向跨语言多模态事实核查的基于偏移量的激活引导方法
translated_abstract: 多模态事实核查面临一个根本性的可及性瓶颈：尽管大型专有模型表现出跨语言鲁棒性，小型视觉-语言模型却在低资源语言上遭受严重且不成比例的准确率崩溃。弥合这一差距传统上需要巨大的模型规模或大量的特定语言微调。在本工作中，我们提出了通过双语推理时技术的偏移恢复方法（ORBIT），这是一种在推理时缓解上述性能崩溃的算法干预手段。ORBIT从平行的声明-证据实例中估计特定跨度的偏移向量，并将其应用于声明和证据的表示上，以针对由低资源证据引发的跨语言退化问题。跨越81种配置的实验表明，ORBIT在低资源设置下显著恢复了准确率和F1分数，并将校准偏移范数揭示为一种诊断性代理指标，同时优于基于翻译的方法。
tldr: 提出了推理时算法干预方法ORBIT，通过从平行声明-证据实例中估计偏移向量并修正声明与证据表示，在不需微调的情况下显著恢复小型视觉-语言模型在低资源语言上的多模态事实核查性能。
en_tdlr: ORBIT, an inference-time offset-based activation steering technique that estimates offset vectors from parallel claim-evidence instances, substantially recovers the accuracy collapse of small vision-language models on low-resource languages in multimodal fact verification.
